subject: kode-cli
title: Anthropic-internal USER_TYPE branches ('ant', 'SWE_BENCH') in readable TypeScript prove Claude-Code-internals origin, contradicting the cline-lineage lore
one_why: No public bundle or independent clean room needs env branches on Anthropic's internal user-type values; combined with claude-shaped internals (canUseTool, ToolUseQueue barrier, PreToolUse permissionDecision) the v1 codebase almost certainly descends from deobfuscated Claude-Code source (the org's anon-kode route) -- the repo's self-granted Apache-2.0 cannot clear that origin, so treat all portables from this subject as concepts-only until provenance is clarified.

subject: kode-cli
title: Two-tier compaction: disk-offload micro-compact of stale tool results, then snapshot-enriched auto-compact with a fit-aware compression-model fallback
evidence: packages/core/src/utils/microCompactCore.ts:19-22,306-360 (persist old tool_results to disk keeping 400-char refs, keep last 3, fire only when >=20k tokens saved past the warning margin); packages/core/src/utils/autoCompactCore.ts:215-241 (task/skills/MCP/plan-file snapshots inside the summarization prompt), :251-276 (use 'compact' model unless its 90%-context budget can't fit history, else fall back to 'main'), :333-355 (compaction boundary + summary persisted as JSONL record for resume)
one_why: Nuance vs deepagents' reversible-offload tier: the offload is disk-backed with preview refs and a minimum-savings gate so it never churns small results, and the summarizer itself is told which model will have to read the summary -- neither appears in cline's or gptme's tiers.

subject: kode-cli
title: Regex data-loss classifier promotes suspicious Bash commands to a quick-model LLM reviewer; gate failure fails closed only when the command would run unsandboxed
evidence: packages/tools/src/tools/system/BashTool/call.tsx:131-203 (getBashGateFindings -> needsLlmGate -> runBashLlmSafetyGate; on gate error block unless canFailOpen, computed from willSandbox); packages/tools/src/tools/system/BashTool/dataLossRules.ts:355 + 14-category SimpleRule set; packages/tools/src/tools/system/BashTool/llmSafetyGate.ts:138-180 (purpose-built single system prompt, 'quick' model pointer, 300s timeout, </final> stop sequence)
one_why: Because the gate lives in the Bash tool call rather than the permission engine, it still fires under YOLO auto-approval -- a floor that survives the product's own worst default; and tying fail-open to sandbox state makes the two defenses compose instead of both being optional.

subject: kode-cli
title: Single permission chokepoint where deny-rules outrank YOLO and bypassPermissions keeps an explicit opt-out-only write-safety floor
evidence: packages/core/src/permissions/engine.ts:96-133 (bypassSafetyFloor requires KODE_BYPASS_SAFETY_FLOOR opt-in before skipping getWriteSafetyCheckForPath), :344-351 (yolo auto-approves only when shouldPromptUser !== false, so explicit denies still win); packages/core/src/test/unit/bypass-permissions-safety-floor.test.ts; packages/core/src/utils/permissionModeState.ts:7 (ACTUAL_DEFAULT_MODE = 'yolo')
one_why: Most yolo/bypass flags are pure boolean bypasses; kode's precedence ladder (explicit deny > mode auto-approve > safety floor unless env-renounced) is the pattern worth copying -- though the shipped default being yolo (README.md:46 discloses it plainly) is what caps this subject's safety score.

subject: kode-cli
title: YOLO is the factory default: fresh installs bypass all approval prompts; permission checks exist but must be opted into via --safe
evidence: packages/core/src/utils/permissionModeState.ts:7 (const ACTUAL_DEFAULT_MODE: PermissionMode = 'yolo'); README.md:46 ('runs in YOLO mode by default (equivalent to --dangerously-skip-permissions)... we strongly recommend kode --safe')
one_why: Nuance vs gptme's silent fail-open: kode's is loud and documented, and the LLM data-loss gate plus deny-rules give yolo a real floor -- but every unattended first run of the distributed product is still an unapproved shell, and no default mode plus per-feature opt-in can match codex's deny-by-default kernel posture.

subject: kode-cli
title: Trust gate covers only workspace MCP headersHelper; project-defined hooks spawn subprocesses with no trust decision
evidence: packages/core/src/mcp/client/connection.ts:121-124 (checkHasTrustDialogAccepted blocks headersHelper pre-trust); packages/core/src/hooks/executor.ts:31 (spawn(cmd[0], ...) with no trust check); grep -i trust over packages/core/src finds no other gate
one_why: A cloned repo whose .claude/settings.json defines a PreToolUse or SessionStart hook executes attacker-chosen commands on first open -- kode built the right gate (the MCP one) and left the wider hook surface ungated; claurst's fingerprint-keyed project-trust store is the missing piece.

subject: kode-cli
title: No scripted provider drives the loop in CI: provider integration tests silently skip without API keys and the shipped VCR harness has no committed fixtures
evidence: packages/core/src/test/integration/integration-cli-flow.test.ts:17-21 (test.skip when ACTIVE_PRODUCTION_MODELS empty); grep -rln mock.module packages/core/src/test => 2 files; packages/core/src/services/vcr.ts:14-56 (content-hash fixture VCR active under NODE_ENV=test) with no fixtures/ directory in repo
one_why: The unit corps proves permission and hook semantics well, but loop-level properties (approval-iff-policy, parallel tool ordering, compaction mid-loop) have no zero-network end-to-end assertion -- codex/cline/kimi-code's scripted-SSE harness is the ceiling kode is missing, and the half-built VCR shows intent without commitment.

subject: kode-cli
title: CI-enforced zone DAG with a reverse-edge ratchet that may shrink but never grow
evidence: scripts/check-architecture.mjs:12-40 (zone/alias registry), :42-46 ('Known reverse edges are listed separately and may shrink, but new exceptions must not appear unnoticed'); .github/workflows/ci.yml:42-43 ('Architecture boundaries' job step on every push, 3-OS matrix)
one_why: Stronger than openhands' single ban-test: it parses the TS AST against a declared allowed-edge map for nine zones and ratchets legacy violations downward, which is why an agent CLI with 145k LOC has no file over 863 lines and the loop stays host-agnostic.

subject: kode-cli
title: Priority-ranked cache_control allocation inside Anthropic's 4-breakpoint limit, stripping foreign cache markers before placement
evidence: packages/core/src/ai/llm/anthropic/cacheControl.ts:14-85 (system blocks >1000 chars first, then >2000-char documents and the tail block, then forced removal of pre-existing cache_control fields)
one_why: Solves the quiet 'more than 4 breakpoints => provider silently drops caching' failure that most subjects ignore, but placement is length-heuristic with no monotonicity invariant across turns -- unlike smelt's fuzzed cache-prefix stability, so it earns nuance, not a new pattern.
